compiler_spec.usage: Locked BfdArchitecture initialization over examples/curl; archid asserted as x86:LE:64:default:gcc by the C++ fixture

analysis_options.fixture_model: Production TypeFactory of the BfdArchitecture over examples/curl; each fixture type built exactly once under a unique fixture_nres_* name (a second getTypeStruct/setFields round on a completed name throws 'Trying to alter definition of type', type.cc:3421-3423). The set.* cells call TypeFactory::setFields with an explicit newSize; grammar.* cells derive newSize/newAlign via TypeStruct::assignFieldOffsets on offset=-1 fields exactly as CParse::newStruct does; dec.* cells feed equivalent XML (3 unnamed <type size="1"> carry name="oct1" on the Rust side; names are outside every compared observation) through the public TypeFactory::decodeType entry with inline <type> children (no <typeref> ids)
analysis_options.type_construction: All 15 records observe Datatype::needsResolution() ? 1 : 0 on the factory-owned object. set.single.offset proves the OFFSET is not part of the condition (single long@4 in an 8-byte struct still sets the flag); set.single.notfills proves an explicit newSize larger than the field keeps the flag clear; arr.factory vs the get_array twin proves the inline TypeArray ctor arm (type.hh:937-944) fires on the factory path too; ptr.ptrptr proves the calcSubmeta inheritance never passes through a second pointer level
analysis_options.normalization: none: raw needsResolution() bits, no id/pointer normalization (no temporary ids are compared)

binary.source_policy: WIP live-tree runner consumed the working-tree examples/curl; the integration runner should re-pin to the base-commit Git blob (34a3febf blob 4e26a362f92f1961bab63000215a84b4d7212dd, sha256 4ee4002baf3525d9fef062f9fcb9b7a9a890509b8bc5211740d0155d7c6b5d1a) exactly like run_printc_symbol_decl_oracle.sh and regenerate expected_stdout_sha256 under that input

cases.covers: TypeFactory::setFields explicit-newSize matrix: single-field-fills sets the flag (type.cc:1569-1571); single-field-notfills (explicit newSize 8 over an int4 field) stays clear; single field at offset 4 whose type size equals newSize still sets the flag (the offset is NOT examined); two fields never set it

CParse::newStruct path: assignFieldOffsets derives newSize from the fields (grammar.cc:2798-2799), so a single long field yields derived size 8 == field size -> flag set; two ints -> clear. This is the cell Rugra's size-deriving set_fields models
XML decode path: TypeStruct::decodeFields tail single-field arm against the decoded size attribute (fills -> 1, notfills size=12/int4 -> 0, multi -> 0) and TypeArray::decode arraysize==1 arm -> 1
TypeFactory::getTypeArray(1, int): the inline TypeArray ctor arm (type.hh:937-944) sets the flag on the factory path as well -> 1

TypePointer::calcSubmeta needs_resolution inheritance (type.cc:1051-1052): pointer to the single-field-fills struct -> 1; pointer to that pointer -> 0 (never through a second pointer level); pointer to long -> 0
TypeUnion ctor starts type_incomplete|needs_resolution (type.hh:551) and TypeUnion::setFields (type.cc:2002-2009) never touches flags -> 1

grammar.overfire: an XML-decoded UNROUNDED struct (size 5, align 4, alignSize 8) as a single grammar field — Ghidra's assignFieldOffsets newSize is calcAlignSize(8,4)=8 != 5 so the flag stays CLEAR (a naive max(offset+getSize) derivation would fire); grammar.nested: inner single-field struct flags, and an outer whose single field IS that inner (size 4 == derived newSize 4) flags too

calcSubmeta runs at pointer construction only: a pointer built while the struct is still an incomplete stub never inherits (stub=0, struct=1 after definition, cached same-name pointer stays 0, differently-sized new pointer inherits=1)

decodeFields overlap throw-out (second field dropped, first survives; the survivor then fills the struct -> flag set, complete) and the incomplete residue (no fields -> incomplete stays set for both size=8 and old-style size=0)

decode rejection texts verbatim: 'Fields are out of order', 'Field z does not fit in structure <name>', 'Bad field data-type for structure: <name>', and the TypeField ctor's 'name attribute must not be empty in <field> tag' firing before the decodeFields void check for both the name and name+void documents

input_model_difference: Ghidra drives its real production TypeFactory inside the BfdArchitecture (tree/nametree cross-references, findAdd dedup); the Rust fixture drives a standalone TypeFactory::new(8) with the same construction calls. The observable compared is the needs_resolution flag bit on each factory-owned type, which does not depend on the tree plumbing
